title: Vignette: Intro to healthiar
text: summarize_uncertainty() assumes following shapes distributions simulations: Relative risk: values simulated based optimized gamma distribution, fits well relative risks positive distributions usually right-skewed. gamma distribution parametrized mean equal central relative risk estimate (rate= shape/rr_central). shape parameter optimized using stats::optimize() match inputed 95% confidence interval bounds, stats::qgamma() used evaluate candidate distributions. Finally, n_sim relative risk values simulated using stats::rgamma(). Exposure, cutoff, baseline health data duration: values simulated based normal distribution using stats::rnorm() mean = exp_central, mean = cutoff_central, mean = bhd_central mean = duration_central standard deviation based corresponding lower upper 95% exposure confidence interval values. standard deviation calculated (upper−lower)/(2*1.96)(upper-lower)/(2*1.96), since normal distribution 95% CI spans approximately two standard deviations either side mean. Disability weights: values simulated based beta distribution, disability weights beta distribution bounded 0 1. beta distribution best fitting inputted central disability weight estimate corresponding lower upper 95% confidence interval values fitted using stats::qbeta() (best fitting distribution parameters shape1 shape2 determined using stats::optimize()). purpose, partly adapted R function prevalence::beta_expert permission one authors (Devleesschauwer et al. 2022). Finally, n_sim disability weight values simulated using stats::rbeta(). stability 95% confidence interval, large number simulations (e.g., 10,000) recommended practice. example uses n_sim = 100 brevity.

title: Vignette: Intro to healthiar
text: life table methodology attribute_lifetable() follows tool AirQ+ (2020), described detail Miller Hurley (2003). generalized formulas, assume fixed fraction life lived (fraction_lived = 0.5), based foundational work Chiang (1984). short, two scenarios compared: scenario exposure level specified function (“exposed scenario”) scenario exposure (“unexposed scenario”). First, entry mid-year populations (first) year analysis unexposed scenario determined using modified survival probabilities. Second, age-specific population projections using scenario-specific survival probabilities done scenarios. Third, subtracting populations unexposed scenario populations exposed scenario premature deaths/years life lost attributable exposure determined. expansive life table case study available report Miller (2010). Use two arguments approach_exposure approach_newborns modify life table calculation: approach_exposure "single_year" (default): Population exposed one year (year analysis) attributable health impacts reflect single-year snapshot. Applicable deaths. AirQ+ approach deaths 2025. "constant" : Population exposed every year, .e. air pollution exposure sustained across full projection horizon attributable health impacts projected cumulated across full lifetime period. Applicable deaths YLL. AirQ+ approach YLL 2025. approach_newborns "without_newborns" (default): Population year analysis followed time, without considering newborns born. "with_newborns": year year analysis n babies born, n equal (male female) population aged 0 provided argument population. Note: Although healthiar alligns methodologically AirQ+, results using life table can marginally differ (e.g. around 0.06% 2,600 attributable deaths). minor variance might arise (least partly) rounding issue. AirQ+ might apply intermediate column-level rounding, healthiar .
